messages.subject: Re: R crashes instantly on calling 'microclimate' function
messages.subject_clean: R crashes instantly on calling 'microclimate' function
messages.body_plain:
Dear Conor Waldock,

I have never come across that error... However, I have seen in several forums that the same error (segfault error) can happen in ggplot2 and other packages. Thus, I am not sure that that problem comes from Fortran... In some forums advice uninstalling and re-installing all R-packages. It is quite easy using this code:

ip <- installed.packages()
pkgs.to.remove <- ip[!(ip[,"Priority"] %in% c("base", "recommended")), 1]
sapply(pkgs.to.remove, remove.packages)

Here you have the link to one of the forums where people adviced uninstalling/reinstalling:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25672974/caught-segfault-error-in-r

Hope it helps! Cheers,
Urtzi

messages.subject: Error calling micro_global()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm just getting started using NicheMapR, and have installed and loaded the NicheMapR, as well as the other packages needed, and downloaded climate data using get.global.climate(), into a directory (same as where the script is).

But calling:
> micro_global()

gives:
extracting climate data
extracting soil moisture data
running microclimate model for 12 days by 1 years at site Madison, Wisconsin USA
Error in dyn.load(paste(lib.loc = .libPaths()[1], libpath, sep = "")) :
  unable to load shared object '/Users/Jennifer_Sunday/Library/R/3.3/library/NicheMapR/libs/MICROCLIMATE.so':
  dlopen(/Users/Jennifer_Sunday/Library/R/3.3/library/NicheMapR/libs/MICROCLIMATE.so, 6): image not found

I'm wondering if this is a common recognizable error having to do with my choice of directory. I was unsure of what directly to use for the climate data download - it is currently in the same directory as the package and the R script, although when R unzipped it, the report said "folder location has been saved into  /Users/Jennifer_Sunday/Library/R/3.3/library/gcfolder.rda".

I'm sure this is something basic that I am missing but I haven't seen it in the posts.

Thanks for any guidance!

Jenn

messages.subject: Re: Error calling micro_global()
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jennifer Sunday,

I have not seen that error before, and Michael Kearney may give you a better advice than me... However, I noticed that the error you reported made reference to the MICROCLIMATE.so fortran file, and not to the folder where you stored the climate data. In fact it seems that the micro_global() function successfully extracted climate data (first two lines after running the function), and then failed when trying to run the microclimate fortran program.

Can you check whether you have the MICROCLIMATE.so file located where it should? If you are a mac user, the path should be something similar to this:

/Library/Frameworks/R.Framework/Resources/library/NicheMapR/libs

Other people have reported a similar error for other R-packages (https://github.com/apache/incubator-mxnet/issues/771) and they fixed it by uninstalling/re-installing, after finding a compilation issue...

Hope this helps!
Cheers,
Urtzi

messages.subject: new version of the NicheMapR microclimate model and Linux compilations
messages.subject_clean: new version of the NicheMapR microclimate model and Linux compilations
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,

I've just released new OSX and Win binaries of the NicheMapR package as a version update, with the details below. Also, thanks to Rafael Schouten we now have an operational compilation for Linux (you can get this from github).

All the best,

Mike

This new release includes a correction and some additional features.

The correction is to the soil moisture algorithm. The value in Campbell's program 11.1 for VP (saturation vapour density) is fixed at the value for 20 degrees C and this was copied into the microclimate model code. However, it should vary with temperature and this correction has now been made (using the WETAIR function internal to the microclimate model). It will affect near surface (<5 cm) soil moisture calculations in particular.

The additional features are to make the following parameters from the soil moisture model available to the user to alter: root radius, resistance per unit length of root and leaf, critical leaf water potential for stomatal closure, stability parameter for stomatal closure equation, maximum allowable mass balance error for soil moisture, maximum iterations for mass balance of soil moisture.

Also, the wavelength-specific solar radiation can now be outputted if required, with the option to undertake a more intensive calculation of the UV wavelengths if desired.

Finally, the model output now includes the snow temperature profiles in the sun and the shade (sunsnow and shadsnow) as well as plant outputs from Campbell's Program 11.1 (transpiration rate, leaf and root water potentials in the output matrices plant and shadplant).
